answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity graph: to transact, an agent locks a stake forfeited if peers detect a duplicate persona, and every new edge must be co-signed by two already-staked agents. Because a Sybil farm needs one bond per fake identity plus two independent vouchers each, cost grows linearly with cluster size instead of staying fixed. A lone agent on a quiet island can still pay one bond and join, but a forged crowd must fund a whole ridge of bonds and vouches, and a sonnet-length audit trail of these co-signatures makes the cluster obvious to graders.
